source.title: Retroactive modulation of spike timing-dependent plasticity by dopamine.

confidence_rationale: Canonical experimental demonstration of a synaptic eligibility trace: a delayed dopamine signal retroactively converts STDP depression to potentiation, solving the distal-reward credit problem. Directly grounds the biological mechanism for ARC-063 element (iv) per-action evidence-trace credit. Held below top band because it credits a SYNAPSE, not a labelled rule.
failure_signatures: The credited unit is a synapse with a ~1s eligibility window, not an abstract rule; ARC-063's rule-level evidence-trace credit is an extension of this synaptic mechanism, not a demonstrated rule-level instance.
Hippocampal slice + NMDA/PKA-dependent; whether the same retroactive-credit mechanism operates on cortical/PFC rule_state representations is untested here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Dopamine can retroactively convert hippocampal timing-dependent synaptic depression into potentiation, acting on a pre-established synaptic eligibility trace (NMDA + cAMP/PKA dependent), thereby associating specific experiences with behaviourally distant rewarding outcomes -- a biologically plausible solution to the distal reward problem.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-063 element (iv) -- structured per-action evidence-trace records -- requires a mechanism by which a delayed outcome/prediction-error assigns credit back to the rule that was active when the action was taken. The synaptic eligibility trace is the biological substrate of exactly that retroactive credit: a trace laid down at rule-use time that a later dopaminergic/PE signal converts into a lasting update.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The eligibility trace here credits an individual synapse over ~1s, not a distributed CandidateRule. REE assumes the same retroactive-credit principle can be lifted to rule-level evidence records; the lift is mechanism-grounded but the rule-level target is not demonstrated in this paper.
mapping.source_context: Mouse hippocampal slice electrophysiology (spike-timing-dependent plasticity + dopamine).

confidence_components.notes: High-quality eLife mechanism paper. Mapping/transfer discounted for synapse-vs-rule target and slice-to-system transfer.
